policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 11:2 has no vocative: 'Now I praise you that ye remember me'. The added ἀδελφοί would appear as 'brethren', which ASV renders wherever it stands; its absence excludes r01.
Presence or absence of the article with Χριστοῦ leaves 'the head of Christ is God' unchanged; English has no correspondent for the Greek article here.
αὐτῆς and ἑαυτῆς both yield ASV 'her head'; the simple/reflexive possessive distinction is not marked in the English.
The article before γυνή is not separately rendered; ASV 'but the woman is the glory of the man' reads the same either way.
ASV 11:11 orders the clauses woman-then-man: 'neither is the woman without the man, nor the man without the woman', matching γυνὴ χωρὶς ἀνδρὸς οὔτε ἀνὴρ χωρὶς γυναικὸς and not the reversed r01.
ASV opens 'Doth not even nature itself teach you' with no disjunctive, but an initial ἤ resuming the preceding question is routinely left unrendered in English, so the absence does not exclude r01.
ἡ φύσις αὐτή and αὐτὴ ἡ φύσις both give 'nature itself'; Greek word order within the phrase is not recoverable from the English.
ASV 11:15 reads 'her hair is given her for a covering' with an unitalicized dative 'her', rendering αὐτῇ; the base reading without αὐτῇ leaves that word unaccounted for.

ASV 11:17 has the participle on the charging and the finite verb on the praising: 'But in giving you this charge, I praise you not', i.e. παραγγέλλων ... οὐκ ἐπαινῶ. Treg's παραγγέλλω ... οὐκ ἐπαινῶν would invert both.
ASV 11:19 renders the conjunction: 'For there must be also factions among you'. 'also' corresponds to καί, which r01 omits.
'What shall I say to you?' fixes English order and cannot distinguish εἴπω ὑμῖν from ὑμῖν εἴπω. The three notes on this verse are alternative_rendering and bear on English wording only.
παρεδίδετο and παρεδίδοτο are orthographic variants of the same imperfect passive; both give 'he was betrayed'. The verse note is an alternative_rendering ('Or, delivered up') and decides no reading.
ASV 11:24 goes straight from 'and said' to 'This is my body'; the added Λάβετε φάγετε would appear as 'Take, eat', and nothing in the English corresponds to it.

ASV text reads 'which is for you' without a participle, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read is broken for you' relegates κλώμενον to the margin, confirming the base reading stands in the text.
ἐάν and ἄν after ὁσάκις are interchangeable particles here; both yield ASV 'as often as ye drink it'.
As in 11:25, ἐάν and ἄν with ὁσάκις both give 'as often as ye eat'; the English marks no difference.
ASV 11:26 contrasts 'this bread' with a bare 'the cup'; the demonstrative added by r01 (τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο) would have been rendered 'this cup', as it is in 11:25.
ἄχρι οὗ and ἄχρι οὗ ἄν both render 'till he come'; the contingent particle has no English correspondent.
ASV 11:27 reads 'shall eat the bread' without a demonstrative; τοῦτον would have produced 'this bread', which ASV does write in 11:26 where the demonstrative is present.
ASV 11:27 carries a single 'of the Lord', attached to the cup, before 'in an unworthy manner'; the additional τοῦ κυρίου of r01 would give a second genitive with no correspondent in the English.
ASV 11:29 reads simply 'For he that eateth and drinketh'; the added ἀναξίως would appear as 'unworthily' or 'in an unworthy manner', the phrase ASV does use for it in 11:27.
ASV 11:29 ends 'if he discern not the body', with no 'of the Lord'; τοῦ κυρίου would have been rendered, as it is elsewhere in the chapter.
ASV 11:31 opens 'But if we discerned ourselves', an adversative rendering δέ; γάρ would have given 'For'.

The article with κυρίου after ὑπό is not separately rendered: 'chastened of the Lord' reads the same with or without τοῦ. The verse note is an alternative_rendering about clause attachment, not a reading.
ASV 11:34 begins 'If any man is hungry' with no connective, but an unemphatic δέ is regularly left unrendered at the head of a sentence, so the English does not exclude r01.
